anomalies.observed: The anodes of the three green LEDs D21, D37 and D43 all sit on net /NET0069, and no other pin is connected to that net. Their cathodes are driven through current-limit resistors from the CM4 Ethernet and activity LED outputs, but nothing supplies the anode side.
anomalies.expected: The anode common of these LEDs should return to the +3V3 rail, as the other status LEDs do (for example D30 via R66 to +3V3, and D45 via R7 to +3V3). Without it the LEDs cannot conduct and never light.
anomalies.impact: Three status LEDs (Ethernet nLED2, nLED3 and the PI activity LED path) never illuminate, so the status indication is lost even though the drive signals are present.

anomalies.observed: R45 (130R) runs from the LED cathode K2 (D1 pin 2, net Net-(D1-K2)) to /NET0010. That same net is the anode A2 (D1 pin 4) and the output of U10. The companion cathode resistor R30 correctly returns to GND.
anomalies.expected: The second LED cathode resistor should return to ground, as R30 does for K1. Otherwise LED2 forms a loop from the driver output back to itself and cannot light.
anomalies.impact: LED2 of the dual indicator D1 is effectively non-functional and its drive loop is shorted back onto the buffer output.

anomalies.observed: The isolated CAN transceivers U19 and U20 have their GND2 (isolated-side ground, pin 5) tied to the same GND net as the board ground (pin 4, GND1). The CAN connectors' ground pins and TVS clamps also sit on that GND net. No separate isolated ground net exists in the netlist.
anomalies.expected: The CA-IS3050G is an isolated transceiver. Its secondary side (VCC2, GND2) should be referenced to an isolated ground that is separate from the board GND, as the specification describes isolated CAN buses.

evidence.quote: two isolated CAN buses (`CAN0`, `CAN1`), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller ... through an isolated CAN transceiver

anomalies.impact: The galvanic isolation the design relies on is defeated, so ground loops and fault paths from the motor-side CAN bus reach the controller board ground.

parsed.summary: The netlist shows several suspicious connections; the most likely is that the anodes of D21, D37 and D43 are left on a net with no supply, so those LEDs cannot light. I also flag the dual-LED cathode resistor R45 returning to its own driver node and the isolated CAN transceivers' GND2 sharing board GND. Confidence is moderate, since some of these may be original design choices.
